title: Wire ISO post: I and J are rounded apart from the written start, so the two arc radii can differ by more than 0.002 mm

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

The wire ISO post writes `I` and `J` as `fu(c.I - p.StartX)` and `fu(c.J - p.StartY)`. It rounds the increment from the unrounded start point. The control adds the increment to the written (rounded) start. Thus the centre that the control reads moves by up to one output step on each axis, and the end point is also rounded.

In inch the post writes 4 decimals (0.00254 mm per step). The start radius and the end radius that the control calculates can then differ by about 0.005 mm. In mm the difference can reach about 0.002 mm. The GF AgieCharmilles ISO programming manual gives an arc check of 0.002 mm, and the control stops with an alarm above it.

## Expected

- `I` and `J` are calculated from the written start and the written centre.
- Inch output uses 5 decimals, as the control's inch input permits.
- The radius difference of the written words stays at or below 0.002 mm, or the post refuses the arc by name.

## Evidence (upstream main `eafe6aec6`)

- `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps:105`: `fu()` writes 4 decimals in inch.
- `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps:439-447`: the arc block.
- Not the same defect as #3474 (an arc that reads as a full turn).

Workaround: post the program in mm.

Found by the post audit against the GF AgieCharmilles manuals (#4130).

## Done means

A test posts small inch and mm arcs. It calculates the two radii from the written words and checks that they differ by no more than 0.002 mm.
